guarantees.claim: On reset (rst_ni low), msg_buf and msg_strb are forced to all zeros.

When en_msgbuf is high (and not in reset), for each share i from 0 to Share-1, msg_buf[i] captures the lower (MsgWidth-8) bits of msg_data_i[i], and msg_strb captures the lower (MsgStrbW-1) bits of msg_strb_i.
When clr_msgbuf is asserted and en_msgbuf is low (and not in reset), msg_buf and msg_strb are cleared to all zeros.
When rst_ni is high and both en_msgbuf and clr_msgbuf are low, msg_buf and msg_strb retain their previous values.

assumptions.claim: MsgWidth must be >= 8 and MsgStrbW >= 1 to keep slice ranges non-negative; the widths of msg_buf[i] and msg_strb must match the slice widths to avoid truncation or extension.
assumptions.risk: Compilation/synthesis failure or width mismatch leading to data corruption.

assumptions.claim: msg_data_i and msg_strb_i must be stable and valid during the clock edge when en_msgbuf is asserted.
assumptions.risk: Captured data may be corrupt if inputs change synchronously with the clock edge.

assumptions.claim: The external logic must be aware that en_msgbuf takes priority over clr_msgbuf; when both are asserted, the clear is suppressed.
assumptions.risk: If a simultaneous clear is intended, the buffer will not be cleared, potentially causing stale data to be used.

uncertain_points.claim: en_msgbuf writes only the lower (MsgWidth-8) bits of each share msg_buf[i]; the upper bits are not updated and may retain sensitive data from previous messages.
uncertain_points.risk: Secret/key material could persist in msg_buf upper bits and be used in subsequent cryptographic operations, leading to information leakage.

uncertain_points.claim: If MsgWidth is set below 8, the slice `0+:(MsgWidth-8)` has negative width, which is illegal in SystemVerilog.
If MsgStrbW is set to 0, the slice `0+:(MsgStrbW-1)` has negative width, which is illegal.
The actual widths of msg_buf[i] and msg_strb are defined outside this chunk; if they differ from the slice widths, truncation or zero-extension may occur.
uncertain_points.risk: Data corruption or subtle functional bugs due to width mismatch.
